page: Microsoft Azure D32a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 32 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB per core. It includes 819 GB of bundled local storage, but does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a balanced profile. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25%, while multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average range. Notably, the PassMark memory score is top-tier, ranking in the top 10%. For language model workloads, the server achieves strong text generation speeds with smaller 135M models, though performance drops to the bottom 25% when processing prompts for larger 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32a_v4 offers a balanced resource density, combining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with a substantial local storage allocation. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring a mix of compute, memory, and local disk space without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Recommended workloads include general-purpose web serving, database operations, medium-scale application servers, and lightweight text generation tasks.
